findings.description: SSL 2.0 is enabled on the target. SSL 2.0 is a severely flawed protocol vulnerable to multiple attacks including DROWN and POODLE. It has been formally deprecated since 2011 (RFC 6176).
findings.mitigation: Disable SSL 2.0 in the server configuration. Configure a minimum TLS version of TLS 1.2.
findings.title: SSL 2.0 Enabled

findings.description: The server is vulnerable to Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160). This critical OpenSSL vulnerability allows an attacker to read up to 64 KB of server memory per request, potentially exposing private keys, session tokens, and credentials.
findings.mitigation: Upgrade OpenSSL to a version that includes the fix for CVE-2014-0160. Revoke and reissue all TLS certificates after patching. Invalidate all active session tokens.
findings.title: Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160)

findings.description: The server is vulnerable to the OpenSSL CCS Injection attack (CVE-2014-0224). An attacker performing a man-in-the-middle attack can force the use of weak keying material, potentially allowing decryption or modification of traffic.
findings.mitigation: Upgrade OpenSSL to a patched version. Apply vendor security patches immediately.
findings.title: OpenSSL CCS Injection (CVE-2014-0224)
